title: The PMC Bank – HDIL Fraud
dek: A co-operative bank allegedly hid over ₹4,300 crore in loans to a single struggling real-estate group using thousands of fictitious accounts, wiping out depositors' access to their own savings overnight.

heroStat.label: in loans to HDIL allegedly concealed from RBI oversight

promise.quote: Punjab and Maharashtra Co-operative Bank's loan book, as reported to regulators and depositors, accurately reflects its lending exposure and asset quality.
promise.madeBy: Punjab and Maharashtra Co-operative Bank (PMC Bank) management
promise.role: Urban co-operative bank regulated by the Reserve Bank of India
promise.context: PMC Bank is alleged to have concealed a large concentration of loans to Housing Development and Infrastructure Ltd. (HDIL) and related entities using thousands of fictitious loan accounts, in breach of RBI single-borrower exposure limits.

target.description: Loan exposure reported accurately to the RBI, within regulatory single-borrower and group-exposure limits, with depositors' funds available on demand.
target.standard: RBI prudential norms for urban co-operative banks, including exposure limits and accurate loan classification.

reality.description: The RBI imposed withdrawal restrictions on PMC Bank depositors in September 2019 after the concealed HDIL exposure came to light. Mumbai's Economic Offences Wing registered a case citing losses of ₹4,355.43 crore, while other filings reference a larger figure of roughly ₹6,118 crore. HDIL promoters Rakesh and Sarang Wadhawan were arrested in October 2019; the Bombay High Court granted them bail in 2024, citing lengthy incarceration and delay in trial.

gap.note: A separate, larger figure of roughly ₹6,118 crore for the total fraud also appears in reporting; this investigation has not yet reconciled the two figures and reports the more specifically-sourced ₹4,355.43 crore EOW figure as its headline number.

verdict.summary: Preliminary verdict, pending fuller research: the concealment of HDIL's exposure and the resulting depositor crisis are well documented, and both named promoters have been arrested and charged. This investigation has not yet verified how much of the seized ₹3,500 crore in assets has been liquidated for depositors, or the trial's current procedural status.
